{"evidence":[{"sentence_id":0,"text":"The 1999–2000 NHL season was the 83rd regular season of the National Hockey League.","title":"1999–2000 NHL season"},{"sentence_id":1,"text":" Twenty-eight teams each played 82 games.","title":"1999–2000 NHL season"},{"sentence_id":2,"text":" This was the first season played in which teams were awarded a point for an overtime loss.","title":"1999–2000 NHL season"},{"sentence_id":3,"text":" The New Jersey Devils defeated the defending champion Dallas Stars for their second Stanley Cup championship.","title":"1999–2000 NHL season"},{"sentence_id":4,"text":" During the regular season, no player reached the 100-point plateau, the first time this had happened in a non-lockout season since the 1967–68 season.","title":"1999–2000 NHL season"},{"sentence_id":5,"text":" Also, in the 2000 Stanley Cup playoffs, the New Jersey Devils overcame a three games to one deficit against the Philadelphia Flyers to win the Eastern Conference Finals.","title":"1999–2000 NHL season"},{"sentence_id":6,"text":" This was the first time that this had happened this late in the playoffs also since the 1967–68 season.","title":"1999–2000 NHL season"},{"sentence_id":0,"text":"On the afternoon of 18 January 2017, a major avalanche occurred on Gran Sasso d'Italia, a mountain in Rigopiano, a tourist destination in the province of Pescara, in Southern Italy's Abruzzo region.","title":"Rigopiano avalanche"},{"sentence_id":1,"text":" The avalanche struck the luxury resort Hotel Rigopiano, killing twenty-nine people and injuring eleven others.","title":"Rigopiano avalanche"},{"sentence_id":2,"text":" The avalanche is the deadliest in Italy since the White Friday avalanches in 1916, and the deadliest avalanche in Europe since the Galtür avalanche in 1999.","title":"Rigopiano avalanche"}],"peer_messages":[],"previous_answer":"The Galtür avalanche happened first.","question":"Which Avalanche happened first, Rigopiano avalanche or 1999 Galtür avalanche ?"}
